name: Biochemistry
boundaries: Biochemistry: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: General physical theory of enzyme catalysis
original_dispositions.reason: BCH-01 captures general catalyst design; BCH-02 includes quantitative prediction of molecular behavior. Neither promises arbitrary reactions or universal catalytic perfection.
The mechanism merits a distinct entry; industrial replacement remains a separate engineering question.

Covered in part. Folding, environment and conformational populations fit its predictive scope. A complete account of chaperone networks is not explicitly demonstrated by its current proposed tests and remains a coverage gap. Disease cures are unsupported.
Its tests include molecular switches, binding, conformational populations and perturbations. Zero off-target effects do not follow from mechanistic understanding.
The addition includes collective composition and functional consequences.

Detailed unresolved mechanisms are important, but the historical entry does not establish a distinct general capability at the selected threshold beyond mechanistic understanding of particular systems. Its claims about reversing aging and energy technology require substantial independent breakthroughs.
The entry is framed as experimentally predictive network behavior rather than an assumed universal code.

Not added separately. It is a consequential open mechanistic problem, but the historical entry did not establish that solving it would by itself produce reliable expression of arbitrary membrane proteins. Relevant molecular prediction overlaps BCH-02; insertion machinery and cellular quality-control networks remain incompletely covered.

Electron and proton tunneling are already established phenomena; a broad new paradigm, functional coherence under physiological conditions, or technological impact would need a specific unachieved, experimentally testable claim. The historical entry groups these different questions and overstates their consequences.

BCH-03 addresses constructed self-maintenance and reproduction; BCH-04 addresses a possible route from simple feedstocks. The historical “approximately 150 reactions” figure is unsupported and is not adopted.
